newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG READY FOR SESTRIERE DRESS REHEARSAL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG READY FOR SESTRIERE DRESS REHEARSAL.

text.p: Pernilla Wiberg is treating Saturday's World Cup downhill as a dress rehearsal for next week's world championships in Sestriere.
"It looks like Sestriere," said the Swede, assessing the 2.6 kilometre Fatschas layout. "It is a course for both gliders and technical skiers.
"It's good to have one like this just before Sestriere."
Wiberg wasn't the only skier to spot a resemblance to the world championship piste.

Italy's Isolde Kostner, who shared victory with Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen last weekend on home snow in Cortina, liked what she saw as she posted the fastest time in training runs on Thursday and Friday.
"Many parts of this downhill, particularly the turns and the way it goes up and down, are very similar to the one in Sestriere," said Kostner. "I like it, it will be good training."

The first women's downhill ever staged at Swiss resort will start a busy weekend of racing which also includes a slalom combined on Sunday, the same day the men will be marching in the opening ceremonies in Sestriere.
With a total of 300 points on offer, Wiberg should consolidate her position on top of the overall rankings then move over to Italy and add to her collection of three world championship titles.
But as she has all season, Wiberg refuses to be drawn into speculation about her title chances.
Normally effervescent and talkative, Wiberg was polite but restrained as she answered questions after training, rushing off at the first opportunity.
"I just think about one race at a time like I have all season," said Wiberg, who has also captured two Olympic gold medals.
"Saturday is a downhill and Sunday is a slalom -- that's it. I'll start thinking about the world championships on Monday.
"I won't talk about the overall. I just ski as fast as I can."
That has been fast enough to leave Wiberg 294 points clear of her nearest rival in the overall rankings, defending champion Katja Seizinger of Germany.
So far this season, the Swede has won four World Cup races, two super-Gs and two slaloms.
No matter what the outcome, she will go to Sestriere leading the super-G and slalom World Cup standings as well as the overall World Cup, a prize never before captured by a Swedish woman.
While Wiberg can wrap up the slalom title with a victory on Sunday the she appears more interested in the downhill, the only World Cup discipline in which she has yet to record a win.
Seizinger, the Olympic downhill champion, will be looking to reclaim top spot in the downhill rankings from the surprising Zurbriggen.
Until just last year, Zurbriggen, a 12-year veteran of the Swiss team, had her name listed in the World Cup record book under "great racers without a victory".
But after collecting her maiden win at the end of last season, Zurbriggen's name can now be found atop the downhill standings, clinging to a precarious three-point advantage over Seizinger.
